Today through Wednesday: Primary focus through Wednesday 
continues to be on the expected heat, as well as potential 
impacts from regional wildfire smoke. The Inland Northwest will 
remain under the influence of a strong high pressure ridge 
extending across the Intermountain West from the south-central 
Plains. A weakening shortwave will track from east-central 
British Columbia this afternoon to central Alberta by Tuesday 
morning. This trough will induce a light northerly flow under 
15kts across southwestern BC/Alberta and into northern 
Washington. BUFKIT profiles over eastern WA indicate light, 
variable flow through about 600-500mb until later Wednesday. 
This will allow the overhead smoke and haze mainly from the 
Kaiser Canyon and Modrite fires to linger over the region today 
through at least Tuesday. During periods of deeper mixing in the
afternoon this may bring an increase to surface-level smoke in 
the Spokane area, though the highest smoke concentrations will 
likely be closer to the wildfires themselves. Wildfire smoke 
monitoring via satellite will be challenging to impossible with 
the abundant mid/high cloud cover overhead as upper level 
monsoonal moisture advects into the region. Not out of the 
question that a few light showers/sprinkles occur in the 
vicinity of the WA/ID Palouse or to the south across the Blues. 
The aforementioned ridge will also bring an increasingly hot 
airmass to the Inland Northwest through midweek, with 850mb 
temperatures peaking around +28C to +29C by Wednesday afternoon.
This will translate to daytime high temperatures in the mid 90s
to low triple digits Tuesday through Thursday, with Wednesday 
likely being the hottest day of the week. There remains 
uncertainty in max temperatures in this timeframe due to 
potential cloud cover and wildfire smoke. NBM 25th percentile 
advertises highs well into the mid 90s Tuesday and near 100 
Wednesday, though if wildfire smoke is thicker than anticipated 
in any one location it could prevent the higher end temps from 
being realized. Have issued Heat Advisories with this update for
both Tuesday and Wednesday, though Tuesday's temperatures will 
be marginal across much of eastern WA and north ID compared to 
Wednesday. Ensemble spread in temperatures notably increases by 
Thursday likely due to the higher potential for cloud cover.

Thursday through Sunday: Confidence continues to increase in 
fire weather conditions deteriorating moving later into the week
as the strong monsoonal ridge to the east begins to break down.
A deep longwave trough pivoting southeast from Alaska will 
phase with a stationary secondary trough off the Pacific coast. 
This aggregate trough then weaken as it gradually slides into 
the Inland Northwest over the weekend. Synoptic moisture will 
remain elevated Thursday into early Friday with the EC ensemble 
indicating PWAT anomalies of 125% to 180% in this timeframe, 
highest across the ridges of the Cascades and Blue Mountains. A 
strengthening 80-90kt 250mb jet rounding the base of the 
offshore trough will place portions of the Inland Northwest into
the favorable zone for added lift under the left exit region. 
This may set the stage for one or multiple rounds of scattered 
convection centered on Thursday, potentially as early as 
Wednesday night and lingering into Friday morning. The finer 
details remain a bit murky at this range though cannot rule out 
a combination of wet and dry thunderstorms, with highest chances
across the mountains where greater upslope lift will be 
present. This is particularly concerning not only due to already
higher than average wildfire activity in the region, but 
because the trough sliding through will likely push a dry cold 
front into the region between Friday and Saturday. Long range 
ensembles are in fairly good agreement in this resulting in at 
least a couple of days of dry and breezy conditions, with the 
NBM forecasting sustained winds over 20 mph and gusts to 30-35 
mph east of the Cascades. In all this is shaping up to be a 
situation where Red Flag Warnings may be initially needed to 
cover the lightning threat Thursday, with windy/low RH RFWs for 
Friday/Saturday. Will need to continue monitoring this setup and
consider Fire Weather Watches with future updates. On the plus 
side, the front should also bring some relief from the hot 
temperatures seen earlier in the week, though remaining 
seasonably warm/hot with daytime temps in the upper 80s and low 
90s. /PMP/SGK
